searchText: Are you only syncing proofs for unfinalised blocks? Perfect 🙂 I do it quite differently from sidecars. For sidecars, when syncing (or when synced also), a block won't be imported without the sidecars. For proofs, I import block regardless the proofs (if proofs are missing then the block will be optimistically imported). Every slot, I check all the unfinalised blocks for which proofs are missing, and start to fetch them from peers And when a block has enough proofs, the it optimistic (and is EL validated), then `optimistic` is switched from true to false At the end, the head is non-optimistic, and the node is ready to serve validatord do proofs become more expensive as we have more sidecars? As far as I know, there is no link between (data column) sidecars and proofs. I cited the example of sidecars because we could treat the proofs the same way as we treat sidecars. aka: require them before syncing a block could we actually bundle the proofs into a side car? so that we wouldn't need a new topic to subscribe to? What do you mean exactly by bundling proofs into a sidecar? Into a DC sidecar? An idea could be to send proofs in blobs actually. But subsribing to a new topic is not a big deal IMO (as we do today) Now working on CREL (Completely Remove the Execution Layer) What does this buy you? It seems like another layer of indirection. I'm not super familiar with the concept of a sidecar. Interested to understand more.

excerpts.content: Are you only syncing proofs for unfinalised blocks?

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
I do it quite differently from sidecars.
For sidecars, when syncing (or when synced also), a block won't be imported without the sidecars.
For proofs, I import block regardless the proofs (if proofs are missing then the block will be optimistically imported).
Every slot, I check all the unfinalised blocks for which proofs are missing, and start to fetch them from peers
